name: Maas Podichathu
description: Dried tuna (mas min, the islands' version of Maldives fish) cut into small pieces and mixed with grated coconut, turmeric, onion, garlic and ginger. It is the islands' signature side dish and closely resembles Maldivian mas huni.
how_to_eat: Eat it as a side with rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'maas podichathu' at island guesthouses and local eateries; tourist resorts can arrange it.

name: Mus Kavaab
description: A curry of boneless fish, usually tuna, in a creamy, mildly sweet coconut gravy with onion, garlic, ginger, green chillies and curry leaves. It is one of Lakshadweep's best-known dishes and is linked to Minicoy.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice or parotta.
how_to_order: Ask for 'mus kavaab' at local eateries and guesthouses.

name: Lakshadweep Tuna Curry
description: A spicy curry of fresh tuna in coconut milk with spices. Tuna and related fish make up about 60% of the islands' catch.
how_to_order: Ask for the day's tuna curry at local eateries.

name: Kilanji
description: A very thin crepe of rice flour and eggs from Minicoy, served with a sweet, thin dish of coconut milk, sliced banana and jaggery. It is made for weddings and to welcome guests.
how_to_eat: Dip or soak the crepe in the sweet coconut milk and banana mix.
how_to_order: Ask local hosts or guesthouses on Minicoy; it is mostly made for occasions rather than sold.

name: Octopus Fry
description: Small octopus cleaned, marinated with salt, turmeric and red chilli powder and deep-fried until crisp. It is a popular beach snack, served with green chillies, garlic and a local sauce.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot as a snack or as a side with rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'octopus fry' at local eateries and beach stalls.

name: Kallummakaya Curry
description: Mussels cooked in a spicy, tangy, creamy gravy of coconut milk, tamarind, tomato and curry leaves.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice, appam or idiyappam.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kallummakaya curry' at local eateries.

name: Squid Fry
description: Fresh squid pan-fried crisp with aromatic spices, often served with lime.
how_to_eat: Squeeze lime over it and eat hot.
how_to_order: Ask for 'squid fry' at local eateries.

name: Lobster Masala
description: Lobster cooked in a rich, spiced tomato gravy.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice or bread.
how_to_order: Ask for it at resort and guesthouse kitchens; availability depends on the catch.

name: Mussel Pickle
description: A tangy pickle of local mussels with spices, oil and vinegar.
how_to_eat: Eat a little on the side with rice.

name: Kadalakka
description: A moist, sweet cake of chana dal (split chickpeas), eggs, sugar and cardamom, sometimes with almonds and raisins, spread in a pan and cut into pieces. Also called kadala pathil, it is made for festivals and celebrations.
how_to_eat: Eat a piece as a snack or dessert.
how_to_order: Mostly home-made for festivals; ask local hosts.

name: Unnakaya
description: Mashed ripe banana shaped around a filling of coconut and nuts and deep-fried. Originally from Kerala's Malabar region, it is popular in Lakshadweep, especially during Ramadan.
how_to_eat: Eat it warm as a snack.
how_to_order: Look for it at home kitchens and during Ramadan.

name: Kinnathappam
description: A soft steamed cake of rice flour, jaggery, coconut milk and coconut.
how_to_eat: Cut into squares and eat with tea.

name: Lakshadweep Coconut Halwa
description: A halwa of grated coconut cooked with katti, coconut sap (neera) boiled down to a jaggery-like paste. Islanders have made it for about 80-100 years, and women's groups on every island make and sell it.
how_to_eat: Eat it in small pieces; it is very sweet.
how_to_order: Buy packed halwa from women's self-help group outlets on the islands.
